newsitem.title: INDIA: Fire kills at least 100 Hindu devotees in India.
newsitem.headline: Fire kills at least 100 Hindu devotees in India.

text.p: A raging fire swept through straw shelters at a Hindu convention in eastern India on Sunday, killing at least 100 devotees and injuring 165, authorities said.

The home (interior) secretary of Orissa state, S.C. Hota, told Reuters in the state capital Bhubaneshwar that some 12,000 people were attending the conference in Baripada town when the blaze tore through thatched huts erected for the event.
"Between 100 and 110 is the approximate number," Hota said.

He said strong winds fanned the fire, which broke out at about 3:30 p.m. (1000 GMT) and swiftly engulfed the camp in Baripada, 220 km (135 miles) north of the state capital and about 175 km (110 miles) southwest of Calcutta.
The blaze was believed to have been caused by either a short circuit or a gas cylinder that exploded, he said. Many of the bodies were charred beyond recognition.
Most of the victims were men napping after lunch at the national convention, dedicated to the memory of the Hindu guru Nigamananda, Hota said.
"The number of exits at the camp was very limited," Hota said, noting that the shelters were made out of straw. "That was a problem."

Two fire tenders at the camp were pressed into service but were unable to contain the raging flames, he said. The state government ordered an administrative inquiry into the fire, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Women and children attending the convention which began last Thursday were in a separate area of the camp, he said. PTI said the conference was scheduled to last three days.
A total of 165 injured were taken to the district headquarter hospital, Hota said. One died in hospital and two were discharged.
Forty-three doctors were attending to the injured, and a medical team with special equipment was driving from Cuttack city, 175 km (110 miles) to the south, Hota said.
It was believed to be the deadliest fire in India since about 425 people died when a blaze ripped through a school prize-giving ceremony in the northern town of Dabwali in December 1995.

Police believed the fire in Dabwali was started by a short circuit under a tent, decorated in synthetic silk which quickly caused the fire to flare up. Most of the victims were children aged between four and a half and 14.
PTI quoted Orissa chief minister J.B. Patnaik as saying he had ordered the payment of 25,000 rupees ($700) to the families of the Baripada victims and 10,000 ($280) to the seriously injured.
Earlier, local news agencies said 200 people were killed and several hundred injured. Hota said the initial estimates appeared to have been exaggerated.
PTI said the fire set off a stampede among panicked devotees at the convention.
